content.comment_body: Hello, I managed to write to the [network input] using the node 'S7 OUT'. To do this, I simulated the presence of a remote device by entering a non-existent IP address from my network setup and chose to read the value from a remote device (with parameters like remote TSAP 01.00, VB 0 Bit 0). As a result, I could use the variable DB1,X1246.0 from Node Red and it functioned correctly. However, selecting 'local variable memory (VM)' in the [network input] properties did not work. The device connection uses: Transport Ethernet (ISO on TCP), IP x.y.z.b, port 102, rack 0, slots 2. Is there a way to achieve this without the workaround? Thank you.
Have you enabled S7 access in the file properties of the [product_name] diagram? You can check under: File > Properties > Offline Settings > General.

My device has the article number [article_no], and in [product_name] Soft Comfort, selecting '[product_name] 8.3' hardware (to match your configuration) results in an online test saying the hardware doesn't match the connected unit. I am currently using version '[version_no]', is this correct? Apologies, I'm new to programming. Is this the appropriate section of the forum or should I post in 'communication' instead?

Your device with article number [article_no] isn't a [product_name] 8.3. It's actually a [product_name] 8.2 without display, so you need to select '[product_name] 8.1 & 8.2 ([version_no])' in the hardware selection if you use [product_name] Soft Comfort V8.3.x. With a [version_no], enabling S7 access in the file properties isn't possible.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to write to the 'network input' of a [product_name] device using Node Red, but are facing issues depending on hardware versions and software options. The workaround involves simulating a remote device, and there's confusion due to mismatched hardware and software versions. Users are frustrated by compatibility problems, unclear error messages, and restrictions on S7 access for certain device versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to write seamlessly to 'network input' memory from Node Red, without hardware constraints or workaround solutions, and want configuration between software and hardware to be straightforward.
